subject: ClearHarbor production: intermittent TCP stalls across private link (routing + GWLB insertion)
messages:
From: Alex Carson <alex.carson@clearharbor.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@clearharbor.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Intermittent stalls for ClearHarbor private-hosted pods (post-GWLB insertion)

Hi Marissa —

We started seeing production traffic intermittently stall after we routed egress through the partner GWLB appliance you recommended during the private deployment. Symptoms: short-lived TCP hangs (~3–12s) on large POSTs (>= 8MB), retries at the application layer, and occasional connection resets. The issue only affects traffic between ClearHarbor services in our VPC and your on-prem connector (no issues to public endpoints).

We captured two things attached: a traceroute showing a path change and a short tcpdump around a failure. Initial notes from our infra team: the DF bit appears set on bigger frames, and MSS negotiation shows peers agreeing to 1448 but we still see retransmit bursts.

Could Redwood help triage? We suspect GWLB insertion + MTU/GSO interaction + route propagation priority but want your guidance because traffic flows work fine for smaller payloads.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Carson
Network Lead, ClearHarbor

Attachments: chb_traceroute_04-18.txt, chb_edge_tcpdump_04-18.pcap

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Intermittent stalls for ClearHarbor private-hosted pods (post-GWLB insertion)

Looping in SRE and NetEng — Vivek/Rishi, tagging Grace for customer-facing updates. Alex, thanks for the capture and summary, this looks like a classic MTU/GSO/GWLB interaction but I want us to validate a few hypotheses before we make config changes.

Quick plan:
- Rishi: please review the tcpdump for DF and packet sizes, confirm if we're seeing large L3 frames with GSO on the sender side and whether the GWLB appliance is fragmenting vs dropping.
- Vivek: check our connector host kernel offload settings (GSO/GRO/TSO) and any MSS clamping we apply on the VPC peering attachment. Also verify the SNAT pool / ephemeral port exhaustion metrics for the connector.
- Grace: prepare a short message for ClearHarbor with temporary mitigation steps (MSS clamp, disable offload on connector NIC, or route around GWLB) and expected tradeoffs.

I'll open a Jira (CHB-4521) and put the customer's logs there. If anyone needs temporary access to our private deployment logs, I'll grant it through the DRP.

Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Carson <alex.carson@clearharbor.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T10:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent stalls for ClearHarbor private-hosted pods (post-GWLB insertion)

Marissa — quick read of the pcap:
- I see the 3–12s stalls correlated with repeated duplicate ACKs and retransmits where MSS was negotiated at 1448. However, the sender is sending large segments (GSO) that the inline GWLB appliance is not rewriting. There are multiple retransmit bursts immediately after the packet crosses the GWLB hop.
- TCP segments have the DF bit set and we see ICMP Fragmentation Needed (Type 3, Code 4) from the GWLB appliance IP in a few traces — but those ICMP responses are intermittently rate-limited by the appliance and sometimes not forwarded to the source.
- No obvious SNAT exhaustion in the time window, but ephemeral ports for the connector jumped temporarily during the incident (possible spike).

Hypothesis: the GWLB insertion creates an MTU that is smaller than the path MTU; because GSO aggregates large frames and the GWLB doesn't handle or propagate ICMP consistently, the sender keeps pushing GSO-sized frames, causing stalls.

Immediate suggestions:
1) Apply MSS clamp (set MSS to 1300) on the connector-facing route table for the ClearHarbor peering attachment so endpoints negotiate a lower MSS.
2) Temporarily disable GSO/GRO on the connector VM NIC (sudo ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off) as a conservative mitigation.
3) As a longer-term fix, work with the GWLB vendor to ensure DF handling + ICMP pass-through and/or move to an inline Transparent NAT that supports re-segmentation.

I'll attach a short config snippet for the connector host and a tcpdump snippet showing the ICMPs.

— Rishi
NetEng, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carson <alex.carson@clearharbor.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@clearharbor.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent stalls for ClearHarbor private-hosted pods (post-GWLB insertion)

Alex / Priya — quick update from our engineering triage (summary + recommended immediate steps):

Summary: Rishi validated the pcap and sees probable GWLB-related MTU/GSO fragmentation behavior. Our connector host also briefly saw a spike in ephemeral ports but nothing sustained. We think the primary cause is large GSO frames crossing an inline appliance that doesn't re-segment or reliably forward ICMP "Fragmentation Needed" messages.

Immediate mitigations (pick one to test, easiest first):
- Option A (low risk): Apply MSS clamp to the ClearHarbor peering route (MSS 1300). This is a routing-level change and should take effect without connector restarts. Expected result: reduces handshake MSS, avoids large segments.
- Option B (conservative): Disable GSO/GRO/TSO on Redwood connector VM NIC for 24 hours while we observe. This requires coordination with your ops but is reversible.
- Option C (workaround): Bypass the GWLB for this customer route (route around via a separate peering attachment); we'll need a short maintenance window to add a static route.

Please tell us which mitigation you'd like to try first. We'll monitor CHB-4521 and subscribe you to alerts. Rishi and Vivek are standing by to apply changes from our side if you authorize.

Cheers,
Marissa

From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@clearharbor.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Alex Carson <alex.carson@clearharbor.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent stalls for ClearHarbor private-hosted pods (post-GWLB insertion)

Thanks team — we validated Option A (MSS clamp to 1300) during a low-traffic window overnight. Initial results: throughput for large POSTs normalized and we saw zero stalls during a 6-hour load test. CPU on the GWLB appliance is unchanged, and connector ephemeral port usage stayed stable.

We will keep the MSS clamp in place for 48 hours and report any regressions. Next steps:
- If stable, we'll keep the clamp and open a vendor case with the GWLB supplier to ask for a permanent fix (ICMP pass-through / resegmentation).
- Redwood: please log a follow-up to track vendor remediation and whether there is a platform-level setting we can expose to customers (e.g., auto-MSS-clamp when GWLB insertion is detected).

Appreciate the quick help — Priya
Priya Singh
SRE, ClearHarbor
